node_labels.n5: Zinc adsorbs as single atoms that seed clusters, which expand into a mesoporous zinc network

node_labels.n15: Zincophilic sites give spacious nucleation and lateral growth to a homogeneous deposit; without them dense nuclei grow at tips into dendrites

node_labels.o1: All strong reflections of the post-plating foil are marked as zinc (#04-0831); two weak ones as titanium (#89-3725)

node_labels.o2: HAADF-STEM of zinc-loaded carbon shows bright zinc at three scales: isolated points, ~1 nm blobs and extended lattice-resolved patches
HAADF-STEM of zinc-loaded carbon shows bright zinc at three scales: isolated points, ~1 nm blobs and extended lattice-resolved patches
node_labels.o3: Lattice fringes of the porous-network region are annotated as Zn(002) = 0.25 nm
node_labels.a1: In the 1 nm sub-image the three circled single-atom features are barely above the noise, with no intensity profile given

node_labels.o4: The N-doped cell shows a localised charge hotspot at the nitrogen, absent at the equivalent site of the pristine cell
node_labels.o22: Annotated Bader charges are -1.1741 e at the nitrogen site N1 and 0.0036 e at the equivalent carbon site

node_labels.o5: Charge transfer to zinc is more negative at every N-doped site (-0.032 to -0.037 e) than at the pristine sites (-0.023 to -0.027 e)

node_labels.o6: Electron accumulation sits as a detached lobe above zinc on pristine graphene but is denser in the zinc-substrate gap on N-doped graphene

node_labels.o7: Binding energies are +0.030/+0.014/+0.029 eV at top/hollow/bridge on pristine graphene and -0.072/-0.089/-0.077 eV on N-doped graphene

node_labels.o8: STEM shows hollow spheres about 500-600 nm across with a bright shell of order 20-30 nm

node_labels.o9: The nitrogen map fills the sphere shell evenly, with no clustering or radial gradient

node_labels.o10: N 1s NEXAFS shows sharp features near 398 and 401 eV for CnC HS and none for C HS

node_labels.o11: After zinc deposition the ~398 eV N 1s feature collapses and the ~401 eV feature becomes the taller of the two

node_labels.o12: The sharp 290.1 eV C 1s feature of pristine CnC HS is absent after zinc deposition, while the 284.9 and 288.3 eV features remain

node_labels.o13: The ~1200 cm-1 Raman feature weakens from the pristine trace at the top of the stack to the zinc-loaded trace at the bottom
node_labels.a2: In all four Raman traces the ~1200 cm-1 window lies within the trace noise, so the claimed decrease is not resolved above it

node_labels.o14: Zinc on CnC HS is a largely flat deposit with sparse protruding platelets; on C HS the surface is a dense mat of sharp platelets
Zinc on CnC HS is a largely flat deposit with sparse protruding platelets; on C HS the surface is a dense mat of sharp platelets

node_labels.o15: CnC HS holds roughly 93-100% Coulombic efficiency to about 205 cycles; C HS data end near 50 cycles after falling to zero at ~40 and ~48
node_labels.a3: The two Coulombic-efficiency records span very different lengths (about 50 vs 205 cycles), so the quoted average efficiencies cover unequal ranges

node_labels.o16: C HS voltage spikes grow from ~2600 min and its trace ends near 4400 min at the 'C HS battery failure' arrow, while CnC HS stays within ~0.03 V to 7100 min

node_labels.o17: The two hosts' plating plateaus nearly coincide at the lowest rate and separate strongly at the highest (about -0.05 V vs -0.10 V)

node_labels.o18: Nucleation overpotentials of 39 mV and 43 mV are marked on the two initial discharge profiles

node_labels.o19: Under a stepped current-density staircase C HS develops large voltage spikes from ~2300 min while CnC HS stays within ~0.05 V to 3500 min

node_labels.o20: Charge and discharge capacity fall from about 1.0 to about 0.9 mAh over 500 cycles and the 1st and 100th cycle profiles nearly overlap

node_labels.o21: A cell stack wired to a multimeter powers a switched-on mobile phone
